classification.difficultyReason: Select allfourwalls and slopingopenfloor, derive its unroundedlength, combine trapezoidal/rectangularareas, convert tilearea units and round up totalrequirement. Unprompted complete physicalarea model connects several taught procedures.

content.prompt: A swimming pool has dimensions as shown in the diagram below.

spec.description: Open pool with rectangular horizontal rim ABCD and sloping floor EFGH. All eight vertex labels, both depth measurements, rim dimensions, right-angle marks at A and D, and dashed hidden edges EF, FG and BF are retained. Ordinary source blue outlines become black; red dashed hidden edges use the standard red.
spec.mathematics: AB=DC=12 m, BC=AD=25 m, AE=BF=1 m, DH=CG=2.5 m. EH and FG are sloping floor edges with horizontal run 25 m and vertical difference 1.5 m. The two long side walls are congruent trapeziums.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied measurements and labels are visible; no calculated floor length or areas are shown.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find the length $EH$, correct to the nearest millimetre.

answer.worked:
The difference in depth is $2.5-1=1.5\text{ m}$. By Pythagoras’ theorem,
$$\begin{align*}EH^2&=25^2+1.5^2\\EH^2&=627.25\\EH&=\sqrt{627.25}\text{ m}\\EH&\approx25.045\text{ m}.\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the approximate number of tiles, each of size $15\text{ cm}\times15\text{ cm}$, required to tile the sides and bottom of the pool. (The tiler may cut the tiles and piece them together.)

answer.short:
Approximately $19\,113$ tiles.

Add the floor and four wall areas, then divide by the area of one tile.
answer.worked:
Use the unrounded floor length from part a. The pool has no top surface to tile.
$$\begin{align*}A_{\text{floor}}&=12\sqrt{627.25}\text{ m}^2\\A_{\text{long walls}}&=2\times\frac{1+2.5}{2}\times25\\A_{\text{long walls}}&=87.5\text{ m}^2\\A_{\text{end walls}}&=12\times1+12\times2.5\\A_{\text{end walls}}&=42\text{ m}^2\\A_{\text{total}}&=12\sqrt{627.25}+87.5+42\\A_{\text{total}}&\approx430.0395\text{ m}^2.\end{align*}$$
Each tile has side length $0.15\text{ m}$.
$$\begin{align*}A_{\text{tile}}&=0.15^2=0.0225\text{ m}^2\\N&=\frac{12\sqrt{627.25}+129.5}{0.0225}\\N&\approx19\,112.8673.\end{align*}$$
Round up to obtain approximately $19\,113$ tiles.
